_doc: ROUTES-1108 slice 1 (plan work/ROUTES-PLAN-1108/plan.md section 3). Generic REFERENCE PORTAL: owner 2026-11-08, "most sites should be treated as portals if through those sites we find links to orginal sources". Read only by vera/reference_portal.py. A portal page yields ONLY identifiers and approved outbound links (DOI, PMCID, PMID, arXiv id, handle, approved publisher landing URL); its prose is never read, stored, scored, logged or shown (the parser has no text handler). Every extracted candidate goes through the unchanged acquisition gates (route, API allowlist, robots/TDM per hop, rate and Crawl-delay, licence, injection, relevance, admission) and is acquired only as full text through a permitted route. A host is usable as a portal only when its row in config/portal_hosts.json is status active with terms permit (default deny: an unknown host is never fetched, only counted as host_unchecked) AND robots.txt allows the page for our own-family group, else * (hyperscaler-only groups are advisory, H13), and states no AI block (vera.selective_fetch.robots_allowed, fail closed) AND none of the exclusion signals below holds AND the host is not in exclusions.hosts. The portal page's own licence is not checked: its text is never evidence. mode: off (nothing runs, no request) | shadow (runs in a background thread with its own deadline, logs counts only, hands NOTHING to acquisition, never delays the caller) | on (synchronous within the acquisition search deadline; candidates merged after every other provider). Ships off (orchestrator 2026-11-08, ROUTES-1108-OFF: shadow would fetch en.wikipedia.org live per question; deny by default). No key, no secret, no env read, no email in any User-Agent.
_dp1_note: D-P1 ruling, CONFIRMED by the owner 2026-11-08 (OD-1108-DISPOSITIONS-2 H7, verbatim: "Sites restricting AI training alone may be link-only discovery portals, provided other applicable restrictions permit it."; this includes User-Agent: __usage_ai-training). A host whose signals restrict only AI training IS allowed as a portal, because extracting links is not training. A host is EXCLUDED as a portal when it has Content-Signal ai-input=no or Content-Usage ai-use=n, a TDM reservation (TDM-Reservation: 1 header, <meta name="tdm-reservation" content="1">, or a /.well-known/tdmrep.json rule reserving the path; an unreadable tdmrep.json counts as reserved), a robots block on our agents (an own-family group, else *, or an AI-block statement; hyperscaler-only groups are advisory, H13), or terms forbidding automated or AI access (portal_hosts.json terms deny). A Bing ai-grounding Disallow binds answer-evidence use only (H11) and does not exclude a portal. Each is a key in exclusion_signals and has a test.
_calibration_note: Every number here is a PLANNER PRIOR or a SAFETY bound, not a decision threshold: the decision gates are the unchanged acquisition gates. max_pages_per_question 4, max_pages_per_host 1, max_links_per_page 50 and max_candidates_per_question 30 (below auto_acquire inline.discovered_max 31) bound work per question; timeout_s 5 and max_page_bytes 4000000 are safety limits (two Wikipedia article pages read 2026-11-07 were 389 kB and 1.51 MB, work/WIKI-REDESIGN-1107/calibration.txt). shadow_deadline_s 30 bounds a background shadow run. relevance.* is copied from config/wiki_ref_portal.json (its calibration note applies: provisional, measured on 2 reference lists and 7 questions on 2026-11-07) and is used only to ORDER COinS references (never to admit). What would change them: the 'autoacq refportal' shadow counts (pages, links, candidates, host_unchecked, excluded_*) and, once on, the downstream relevance-gate pass rate and full-text yield of portal candidates over live questions.
user_agent: VERA-DAR-reference-portal/0.1 (non-commercial educational research assistant; reference-link discovery only; https://github.com/taggm-ghc/vera-dar)
_max_hops_note: OD-1109-SIX (owner 2026-11-09: follow links from portals until arriving at original hosts of sources): caps.max_hops 2 lets a portal page lead to ONE further eligible portal page (another host with an active, terms-permit registry row; robots/TDM/AI signals/rate/Crawl-delay checked per page exactly as for the first page) whose identifiers and approved landing links become candidates; every candidate still goes through the unchanged acquisition gates and is acquired only as full text through a permitted route. Bounded by max_pages_per_question (4), max_pages_per_host and the deadline. A structural bound, not calibrated; 1 restores the single hop.

exclusion_signals._note: true = the signal EXCLUDES the host as a portal. All five MUST be exactly true: validation refuses any other value (fail closed) and vera/reference_portal.fetch_page applies those five checks unconditionally, so they cannot be switched off by config. ai_input_no covers Content-Signal ai-input=no and Content-Usage ai-use=n. AI-training-only signals (ai-train=no, train-ai=n, a __usage_ai-training group) never exclude a portal (owner H7, OD-1108-DISPOSITIONS-2); the former ai_train_no_only switch is removed and validation refuses it.

exclusions._note: A host equal to, or a subdomain of, an entry is never read as a portal and no link TO it is kept, whatever portal_hosts.json says (exclusion wins). A DOI is a separate identifier: a doi.org link to an excluded publisher's work is dropped only when its prefix is in doi_prefixes (10.1101 = bioRxiv/medRxiv, OD-7), checked on every candidate from every adapter; other DOIs go to the unchanged acquisition gates. OpenStax: terms forbid generative-AI ingestion (GENSCI-SOURCES-1108 S3). OAPEN/DOAB: www.oapen.org robots disallows ClaudeBot and anthropic-ai (B2). CERN CDS: Anubis challenge, never bypassed (E1). bioRxiv/medRxiv: preprint policy OD-7. AWS, Nvidia, Microsoft Learn docs: terms forbid automated access (R-050).

classifier._follow_origin_note: OD-1109-ORIGIN (owner 2026-11-09, Follow to any original host (gated)): an on-question reference (COinS title/venue matches the question) on a registered portal page may lead to its ORIGINAL host even when unregistered; the link becomes an ordinary URL candidate read only through vera.web_route (READ gate, public_fetch URL safety with pinned public IPs, robots.txt for our tokens, AI-use / Content-Usage / TDM signals, licence, rate limit and Crawl-delay, redirects only within the target host) and is answer-only (never persisted by this route). Hop budget: the portal page is hop 1 and the original host hop 2 (caps.max_hops); an origin link from a hop-2 portal page is not followed. false restores the registered-landing-only rule.
classifier._note: Deny-all: an href is kept only when it classifies as one of kinds. doi/pmcid/pmid/arxiv/handle use search_providers.ddg_identifier (the shared URL identifier rule); web.archive.org snapshots are unwrapped first (wiki_ref_portal.unwrap_archive); landing = an https URL whose host is in the approved publisher landing-host list (ships empty, so nothing is kept as landing until hosts are approved). Same-site, navigation, social and every other link is dropped. PMID-only references are dropped (they need the Europe PMC id lookup).

openalex_rw._enabled_doc: RETRIEVAL-1109 H-3: off. The owner approved only the Wikipedia title route (D-W1); OD-1108-SRC item 4 keeps keyless OpenAlex for search, not this cited_by reference adapter.
openalex_rw._note: Keyless OpenAlex (OD-1108-SRC 4: no API key). Seeds are the OpenAlex works the acquisition search ALREADY returned (no new search call). ONE call per question at most: filter cited_by:W1|W2|W3 returns the works those seeds reference, with the OA fields, parsed by the shared OpenAlexProvider.parse. Through the shared openalex rate portal (1 req/s, concurrency 1) and the shared daily budget; skipped while the OpenAlex quota cooldown is active; a 429/quota error starts that cooldown and is never retried in the question. Results cached per seed set (cache_ttl_s, cache_max). or_seeds false = only the first seed (one call either way). UNVERIFIED until a recorded response confirms it: OR (|) support in the cited_by filter. run_in_shadow false (SECREV M2): in mode shadow this adapter makes NO call, so shadow never spends the shared keyless budget, holds the shared openalex slot or starts the process-wide quota cooldown; it runs only in mode on.

wikipedia_title._note: No on-wiki search (robots disallows /w/ and /api/ for *). Page URLs are built directly from the question's content terms: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/<Title> as-is, then a naive singular (max_title_tries pages). They go through the same generic page path (registry row en.wikipedia.org, paths /wiki/<Title> only, 1 req/s rate portal wikipedia, robots, signals). OpenAlex-topic Wikipedia links are NOT used in slice 1 (field shape unverified).

generic_page._enabled_doc: RETRIEVAL-1109 H-3: off. Reading arbitrary DDG/OpenAlex result pages as portals was not part of the owner's approval (only the Wikipedia title route).
generic_page._note: Result pages already returned by DuckDuckGo (raw results) and OpenAlex landing URLs. A result that is not usable evidence can still be read as a portal when its host passes eligibility.

arxiv_html_refs._note: slice 2: shares the arXiv Crawl-delay 15 budget with the full-text route

inspire_refs._enabled_doc: PHYS-SUPPLY-1110: on per owner OD-1108-DISPOSITIONS-2 H9 (b), verbatim "Approve (b). Enable INSPIRE-HEP independently of Wikipedia portal activation." (records/decisions.md). Runs only with mode on AND api_permissions inspire_literature owner_switch permit (vera.reference_portal.inspire_permitted). Terms re-read 2026-11-09 (research-reader, summarizer level; work/PHYS-SUPPLY-1110/notes.md): 15 requests / 5 s per IP, 429 when exceeded, wait at least 5 s; metadata mostly CC0; email download not permitted; no full text reconstructed from snippets; robots.txt disallows /api/literature/import but not /api/literature for *. false switches it off.
inspire_refs._note: INSPIRE batch (separate release, after API-ALLOW ships). Owner OD-1108-SRC item 2: API CLEARED for metadata and references only, 15 req / 5 s, CC0 metadata, email fields dropped. ONE literature search per question (size seeds, most cited) returning identifier fields only; each hit's own DOI/arXiv id plus up to max_refs_per_seed reference ids. Through vera.api_permissions.call (entry inspire_literature, rate portal inspire); without the API allowlist module nothing is sent. cooldown_min_s 5 = the documented wait after a 429 (GENSCI-SOURCES-1108 I2); size, max_refs_per_seed, max_query_terms and caches are planner priors (bounds, not decision thresholds; calibrate from 'autoacq refportal' inspire_* shadow counts). Field paths UNVERIFIED until one response is recorded; any other shape yields nothing. Ships enabled false in slice 1; the INSPIRE batch flips it.
